hypothesis: r4 (enc3.h4.x2 + cross.h1.x0.5): the best design gain (+10.6, 145 fixed, 39 broken) among the two-head arms. Hypothesis: the encoder head enc3.h4 carries the cube-position signal too weakly at ×1 and the arm stops short of the cube or overshoots it, so a milder amplification at ×2 plus a half-strength cross.h1 makes the first reach land better; r4's 53 against 30 paired lead over the deviation-gain rival on design seeds is screening, not proof. Expected validation gain 5 to 9 points.
hypothesis_source: hypotheses.md, validation section of 2026-11-24, copied word for word. Written before any validation rollout and after the design results.

evidence_on_the_hypothesis.summary: On the validation seeds the edit passes the validation rule, but the files do not support the written mechanism (a better first reach): the median reach error went up, the gain is as large on the other failures as on the target failures (fixed_by_kind), and the edit breaks successes in the low corner of the square (zones).
evidence_on_the_hypothesis.dial_test_note: design seeds 20000 to 20299, one head at a time, rule in awe/dose.py. The pair itself has no dose response before the test.

chosen_by: stage3/choice.json, the rule of awe/candidates.py, fixed before any validation rollout
limits: Chosen among 8 validation-checked candidates (pooled design and validation net gain). Validation gains of the 8 were 7.6 to 10.4 points, not distinguishable from each other. r6 (three heads) had the largest validation gain (+10.4, the edit +9.2) and r4 the largest pooled net (152 against 150). s1 (one head) was excluded from the choice because only 7 matched random edits exist for it.
